segments.t: latest announcement from SK Hynix lifting sentiment following that global chip
route. The South Korean tech giant planning to buy back 29 billion dollars worth of its own shares.
It is an effort to ease the concerns over the durability of AI spending.
Bloomberg's Neil Kampling joins us now for more. There was clearly a need to do this, Neil,
now that we see stocks rallying. Is this the trick? Is this what companies need to do?
Just start buying back shares. Well, it kind of helps for me, doesn't it?
We have been expecting a buyback announcement for the last couple of weeks, so at least that's
put that concern to pay when they've announced it. It's not necessarily going to end the jitters
around the whole AI spending argument, of course, because whilst they're generating a lot of free
cash flow at the moment, they've also announced significant capex spending. And then there's all
questions around how the accounting treatment will be, whether you're canceling treasury shares, etc.
So it doesn't read to me like a simple way of like a U.S. buyback does in terms of
canceling the stock, etc. So let's wait and see how this plays out. But it's an incremental
positive for the stock in the short term, at least.
